Description: As a potential client, I want the homepage to immediately communicate who owns the portfolio and what kind of work they do, so I can decide whether to keep exploring.
Acceptance Criteria: Homepage renders a strong hero; supporting sections expose professional proof; route composition stays clear.

Description: As a visitor, I want to browse professional experience, so I can understand the owner's background and credibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Experience list and detail routes render CMS-backed jobs; missing states are handled through route/partial boundaries.

Summary: PF-103 Browse skills and related work
Description: As a visitor, I want to browse skills and see related work, so I can connect capabilities to evidence.
Acceptance Criteria: Skills are CMS-backed; skill detail pages exist; related jobs are shown where available.

Description: As a technical reviewer, I want project pages to explain concrete work, so I can evaluate delivery depth.
Acceptance Criteria: Project list and detail routes render from CMS data; project revisions carry structured narrative content.

Summary: PF-201 Store content as structured records
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want content stored as structured records, so updates do not require hard-coding every page.
Acceptance Criteria: Schema includes companies, experience, skills, projects, blog posts, translations, media, revisions, and content entities.

Summary: PF-202 Support CMS content lifecycle statuses
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want content lifecycle statuses, so drafts and testing records can exist without becoming public by accident.
Acceptance Criteria: CMS status enum includes published, hidden, draft, and testing; query layers define visible statuses.

Description: As a content author, I want rich article/project bodies represented as safe structural content, so the site can render complex writing without unsafe raw HTML.
Acceptance Criteria: Structural content schema exists; renderer supports known elements and fallbacks; tests cover filtering and fallback behavior.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want demo seed data, so local and design testing can use repeatable content.
Acceptance Criteria: Seed script exists; structural content stress posts and localized demo content are present.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want the CMS authoring workflow defined before editor implementation, so admin work starts from a coherent model.
Acceptance Criteria: CMS authoring workflow defines current state, first workflow, content priorities, owner-only/source-aware boundaries, data implications, and remaining decisions.

Summary: PF-206 Design owner draft preview publish flow
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want an owner-only draft, preview, and publish flow, so content changes can be reviewed before publication.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR 0011 bounds the owner-only draft, edit, authenticated preview, validate, publish/testing, and audit flow; route/action implementation remains future work.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want media lifecycle decisions before upload tooling, so assets do not become unmanaged storage clutter.
Acceptance Criteria: Media lifecycle defines owner-only intake, provisional storage, metadata, alt text gates, attachments, preview, replacement, retirement, cleanup, and deferred implementation decisions.

Summary: PF-208 Implement owner media upload lifecycle
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want owner-only media upload and cleanup tooling, so project and post assets stay accessible, localized, and reconciled with storage.
Acceptance Criteria: Tooling follows ADR 0012; owner can upload, attach, replace, retire, dry-run cleanup, and avoid deleting referenced assets.

Description: As a visitor, I want localized routes, so I can browse the portfolio in the intended language context.
Acceptance Criteria: Locale route tree exists; invalid locales route to not found; locale request setup is centralized.

Summary: PF-302 Redirect bare blog URLs canonically
Description: As a visitor following an old or bare blog URL, I want to land on the canonical localized post route.
Acceptance Criteria: Bare blog resolver redirects to localized route; translated slugs are indexed.

Description: As a crawler or social preview consumer, I want metadata to resolve from localized CMS records, so previews match the page language.
Acceptance Criteria: CMS modules expose metadata resolution for blog, experience, projects, and skills.

Summary: PF-401 Sign up with portfolio identifier flow
Description: As a reader, I want to sign up with a portfolio-specific identifier flow, so I can interact without the site exposing unnecessary account details.
Acceptance Criteria: Identifier resolution distinguishes username and email paths; signup route and server action exist.

Summary: PF-402 Sign in and sign out reliably
Description: As a returning reader, I want to sign in and sign out reliably, so my visible session state matches server state.
Acceptance Criteria: Better Auth route handler exists; sign-in action creates session; logout refreshes local state; current worktree includes auth-state updates.

Summary: PF-403 Validate and rate-limit auth flows
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want credential validation and rate limiting, so auth flows are harder to abuse.
Acceptance Criteria: Zod validation covers usernames, emails, identifiers, passwords, and sign-up shapes; rate limit table and enforcement exist.

Description: As an authenticated reader, I want to comment on blog posts, so I can engage with technical writing.
Acceptance Criteria: Comments table links to posts and optional users; comments render on posts; composer/action exist.

Summary: PF-405 Preserve discussion after account deletion
Description: As a reader, I want discussion history preserved even if an account is removed, so conversation context does not disappear unexpectedly.
Acceptance Criteria: Comment user foreign key preserves comments after account deletion; rendering has fallback author handling.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want comment moderation states defined before schema changes, so moderation does not become a pile of unrelated flags.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR 0009 defines visible, hidden, and removed soft states, owner-only first actions, schema direction, and non-goals before migration work.

Summary: PF-407 Hide or remove abusive comments
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want to hide or remove abusive comments while preserving thread structure, so discussion stays readable and trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria: Owner-only moderation path is defined; hidden/removed rendering behavior is specified before implementation.

Description: As a reader, I want clear rules for comment editing, deletion, and reporting, so I understand what control I have after posting.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR 0009 defers reader edit, delete, and report controls from the first moderation slice and keeps them as review triggers.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want an owner authorization model before protected tools, so moderation and authoring routes are not guarded ad hoc.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR 0010 defines explicit server-side owner allowlist matching, rejects first-version RBAC, and requires one shared guard for owner tools.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want to decide whether client/private accounts belong in the portfolio, so account scope does not grow without a use case.
Acceptance Criteria: Auth roadmap separates reader, owner, client, collaborator, and public profile account types with decisions.

Summary: PF-411 Connect owner auth to protected workflows
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want owner auth connected to moderation and CMS authoring workflows, so protected tools share one account strategy.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR 0010 defines the shared owner guard strategy and ADR 0011 requires CMS authoring to use it; moderation and CMS implementation still need to call it.

Summary: PF-412 Define user roles for privileged actions
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want user roles to distinguish normal readers from higher-privilege users, so moderation, authoring, and future protected actions do not rely on one-off authorization checks.
Acceptance Criteria: First role vocabulary is documented before schema or guard implementation; initial roles are bounded to Reader, Moderator, and Owner; server-side authorization responsibilities are defined; the plan explains how this evolves from ADR 0010 without breaking reader auth/comment behavior.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want privileged UI islands to render as fast client shells while all privileged data and mutations remain server-authorized, so role-gated controls can feel reactive without trusting client state.
Acceptance Criteria: Permission-gated island pattern is documented; client shell, server capability payload, SSR entry behavior, mutation reauthorization boundaries, and the island-versus-route-gate boundary are defined; FigJam flow PF-DIAG-009 visualizes the pattern; Jira and Confluence links are synced.

Summary: PF-501 Version schema changes as migrations
Description: As the developer, I want schema changes generated as committed migrations, so database evolution is reviewable.
Acceptance Criteria: README documents migration workflow; Drizzle files and snapshots exist; build flow runs migrations before Vercel builds.

Description: As the developer, I want branch-isolated Neon database workflows, so local and preview work do not collide with production data.
Acceptance Criteria: Neon sync script creates/reuses branch-scoped URLs; docs warn about stale env values.

Description: As a maintainer, I want clear architecture boundaries, so future changes can be placed correctly.
Acceptance Criteria: Architecture index and local notes define routes, partials, repeatables, CMS, and DB layering.

Description: As a maintainer, I want automated checks for important behavior, so regressions are caught before deployment.
Acceptance Criteria: Unit tests cover auth validation, auth rate-limit keys, structural content rendering, and blog comments; CI workflow exists.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want source-controlled product analysis, so future work can be planned instead of improvised.
Acceptance Criteria: Analysis directory exists; requirements, stories, traceability, ADR, schema inventory, and API notes are in place.

Description: As a technical maintainer, I want an API surface inventory, so internal routes and server actions are not mistaken for public OpenAPI contracts.
Acceptance Criteria: Inventory lists route handlers, server actions, contract status, OpenAPI triggers, and update rules.

Description: As a technical reviewer, I want a table-level schema catalog, so I can understand database purpose and relationships before reading schema.ts.
Acceptance Criteria: Catalog lists current enums, tables, product purposes, relationship themes, source-of-truth rules, and update rules.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want a Confluence page tree plan, so product and business docs can move out of local files cleanly.
Acceptance Criteria: Page hierarchy maps to local analysis docs; ownership and update rules are defined.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want a Jira setup plan, so stories can be imported with stable labels, epics, and acceptance criteria.
Acceptance Criteria: Jira project fields, issue types, labels, and CSV mapping are documented.

Summary: PF-603 Inventory Figma and FigJam diagrams
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want a diagram inventory for Figma/FigJam, so visual artifacts are created with purpose.
Acceptance Criteria: Required diagrams are listed with owners, source docs, and update triggers.

Description: As a technical reviewer, I want ADR coverage for major decisions, so I can understand why the system evolved this way.
Acceptance Criteria: ADR index exists; future ADR candidates are listed.

Summary: PF-605 Define stakeholder and persona analysis
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want stakeholder and persona analysis, so requirements and content choices are grounded in real audiences.
Acceptance Criteria: Stakeholder map, personas, persona-to-requirement map, and product implications are documented.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want a risk register, so product, technical, process, and tooling risks stay visible before implementation.
Acceptance Criteria: Risk register includes ids, areas, likelihood, impact, mitigations, related docs/stories, cadence, and escalation rules.

Description: As a maintainer, I want a validation strategy, so each future slice has clear evidence before being treated as done.
Acceptance Criteria: Validation layers, done definition, work-type checks, verification commands, focused test coverage, and traceability checklist are documented.

Summary: PF-608 Track external tool setup history
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want external tool setup history, so Confluence pages, Jira keys, and FigJam sections stay traceable to local source files.
Acceptance Criteria: Tool setup plan, execution runbook, Confluence publishing runbook, Jira import history, and FigJam creation log are documented.

Summary: PF-609 Maintain review cadence and decision registers
Description: As the portfolio owner, I want a review cadence, decision log, and open-question register, so product direction stays maintained after setup.
Acceptance Criteria: Release/review cadence, artifact maintenance matrix, decision log, and open questions register are documented and linked from the suite.

Description: As a maintainer, I want a requirements traceability matrix, so requirements, personas, stories, evidence, and verification stay connected as the portfolio evolves.
Acceptance Criteria: Matrix maps FR and NFR ids to personas, Jira stories, evidence, verification signals, coverage gaps, and update rules.

Description: As a potential client, I want clear service entry points, so I can choose the kind of help I need without guessing.
Acceptance Criteria: Conversion path defines service wedges, entry offers, recommended CTA, and page implications.

Description: As a potential client, I want a focused intake path, so I can describe the problem and start a scoped conversation.
Acceptance Criteria: Intake questions are defined; future route/component can collect contact and problem context.

Summary: PF-703 Link proof to service wedges
Description: As a visitor, I want projects and posts linked to service wedges, so I can connect proof to the service I need.
Acceptance Criteria: Content strategy and conversion path define how proof surfaces should support service wedges.

Description: As the portfolio owner, I want a visitor journey diagram, so the conversion path can be reviewed visually before implementation.
Acceptance Criteria: FigJam diagram PF-DIAG-001 includes homepage, proof review, trust check, and action path.

Description: As a potential client, I want service offers to explain fit, scope, outputs, and proof, so I can choose the right first conversation.
Acceptance Criteria: Service offer catalog defines offer ids, buyer signals, included and excluded scope, first outputs, proof surfaces, pricing stance, and intake routing.
